faq.q: Can TallyPrime connect to an online store or app?
faq.a: Yes. TallyPrime can act as a server over HTTP, on port 9000 by default, and accepts XML, and from version 7.0 native JSON, to import and export data. Because Tally usually runs on an office PC, a cloud store needs a small connector on that network to push orders in.

faq.q: Does Tally have a REST API?
faq.a: Not in the usual cloud sense. Tally exposes XML and JSON requests over HTTP on the machine where it runs, and ODBC for SQL Select queries. There is no hosted endpoint on the internet, so you build or buy a connector that talks to the local port.

faq.q: What are the Zoho Books API limits?
faq.a: Zoho's API page lists 100 requests per minute per organisation and daily caps of 1,000 on Free, 2,000 on Standard, 5,000 on Professional and 10,000 on Premium, Elite and Ultimate. Concurrent calls are capped at 5 on Free and 10 on paid plans. Going over returns HTTP 429.

faq.q: Who needs to generate e-invoices in India?
faq.a: Businesses whose aggregate turnover exceeded ₹5 crore in any financial year from 2017-18, for B2B invoices, since 1 August 2023 under notification 10/2023-Central Tax. From 1 April 2025, those with turnover of ₹10 crore and above must report invoices to the IRP within 30 days.

faq.q: Can my app call the IRP API directly?
faq.a: It depends on the IRP and your turnover. GSTN's comparison says the NIC portals offer Direct API registration only at ₹100 crore turnover or more, while some private IRPs are open to all e-invoicing taxpayers. Most SMEs go through their accounting software or a GST Suvidha Provider.

faq.q: What is the SAP Business One Service Layer?
faq.a: It is SAP Business One's web API, built on HTTP and OData. You log in with the company database and user details, get a session cookie, and then read or write business objects such as items and orders. SAP's guide added webhook support in January 2026.

faq.q: Do I need to replace my ERP to sell online?
faq.a: Usually not. All three ERPs here have official ways for other software to read and write data. Replacing the ERP is a bigger, riskier job that is worth doing only if the ERP itself no longer fits the business.

contentHtml:
What ERP integration means for an Indian business

In short: You can connect TallyPrime, Zoho Books or SAP Business One to your website, store or app without replacing them. TallyPrime accepts XML and, from version 7.0, JSON over HTTP on port 9000; Zoho Books has a REST API with OAuth and daily call limits by plan; SAP Business One has the Service Layer, an OData API. If your aggregate turnover has crossed ₹5 crore in any year since 2017-18, your B2B invoices also have to go to the GST Invoice Registration Portal for an IRN, and that step belongs in the same design.

This guide was checked in November 2026, against Tally's, Zoho's and SAP's own developer documents and the GSTN, e-invoice and e-way bill portals, all read on 16 November 2026.

The phrase "without a rewrite" is the point. Most Indian businesses have years of ledgers, stock items and party masters in their accounting system, and an accountant who knows it well. A new app or online store does not need a new ERP. It needs a clean, boring pipe between the two, and a clear rule about which system owns which piece of data.

Three ERPs, three doors

Each of the three systems exposes its data differently. Here is the short version before the detail.

The official integration options for the three ERPs most Indian SMEs use

TallyPrimeZoho BooksSAP Business One
Main doorXML over HTTP; JSON from TallyPrime 7.0REST API, v3Service Layer (OData v3 and v4)
Where it runsOn the machine running Tally, default port 9000Zoho's cloud, India data centre at zohoapis.inOn the customer's server, example port 50000
How you log inNo login on the HTTP port; you control network accessOAuth 2.0, with organization_id on every callPOST to /Login, then a session cookie
Read only optionODBC with SQL Select statementsNot needed; the API readsNot needed; the API reads
Push on changeNot built in; poll, or write TDL to post outWebhooks from workflow rulesWebhooks added in the 2026 Service Layer guide
Published limitsNone stated100 calls a minute per organisation, daily caps by planNone stated in the guide

Source: Tally XML integration and Tally JSON integration and Zoho Books API introduction and SAP's Working with Service Layer guide, read 16 November 2026.

The 'no login' entry for Tally is my reading of the setup steps, which enable the HTTP server and give no authentication step. Treat port 9000 as something that should never face the internet.

TallyPrime: XML, JSON and ODBC

Tally's XML integration page says TallyPrime exposes its data and operations as XML over HTTP and can act as both server and client. To turn it on, you go to F1 (Help), then Settings, then Advanced Configuration, and enable the HTTP Server. The default port is 9000. Every message is an ENVELOPE with a HEADER and a BODY, and the header says whether the request is an Import or an Export.

From TallyPrime 7.0, Tally's JSON page says native JSON is available as a default feature, like XML. If your data is in Tally's native JSON structure, Tally can import it directly, with no extra TDL code. The Tally help site banner said TallyPrime 7.2 was live when I checked.

The third door is ODBC. Tally's ODBC page shows SQL Select statements on Tally collections, such as Select $Name, $ClosingBalance from Ledger. It is good for reports and dashboards. For writing vouchers, use XML or JSON imports.

Two practical limits matter more than the format. Tally has to be running, with the right company open, for the HTTP port to answer. And it usually sits on one office PC or a local server, so a cloud app cannot reach it without a small connector program on that network that pushes data out. That, more than the XML format, is what shapes the design.

Zoho Books: the REST API and its limits

Zoho Books is the easiest of the three to reach, because it already lives on the internet. The API introduction lists a base URL for each data centre, and Indian organisations use https://www.zohoapis.in/books/. Every request carries an organization_id, and access is through OAuth 2.0 with access and refresh tokens.

The limits are published, and they are the thing to design around:

  • 100 requests per minute per organisation.
  • Daily caps by plan: Free 1,000, Standard 2,000, Professional 5,000, and Premium, Elite and Ultimate 10,000.
  • Concurrent calls: 5 on the Free plan, 10 on paid plans as a soft limit.
  • Going over any of these returns HTTP 429.

A store doing a few hundred orders a day fits easily if each order is one or two calls. A sync that re-reads every invoice every hour does not. Zoho Books also supports webhooks from workflow rules, so it can call your app when, for example, a sales order is created, instead of you asking every few minutes. Zoho's page says the daily webhook limit varies by plan.

On GST, Zoho says it is a registered GST Suvidha Provider, and its e-invoicing help describes pushing invoices to the IRP from inside Zoho Books to get the IRN and QR code. If you are on Zoho Books, let Zoho do the IRP step and have your app create the invoice in Zoho, rather than talking to the IRP yourself.

SAP Business One: the Service Layer

SAP's Working with SAP Business One Service Layer guide describes it as an API built on HTTP and OData, exposing full business objects. You log in with a POST to /b1s/v1/Login or /b1s/v2/Login with the company database, user name and password, and get back a B1SESSION cookie; the guide's example shows a session timeout of 30 minutes. /b1s/v1 is OData version 3 and /b1s/v2 is version 4.

The guide's history table has a change worth knowing about: version 1.28, dated 7 January 2026, added basic webhook support with event subscription, notification delivery and retries, and version 1.29 in July 2026 added filters on those events. If your partner's integration still polls SAP every few minutes, ask whether your version supports webhooks.

Like Tally, Service Layer usually runs on the customer's own server, so a cloud app needs a VPN, an allow-listed address or a small relay. Each session is tied to one company database, which matters if you run several companies.

GST e-invoicing: who must, and how the IRP works

If you are above the threshold, an integration that creates invoices has to deal with e-invoicing. The rules I verified:

The e-invoicing rules that shape an integration, as published

RuleWhat it saysSource
ThresholdMandatory from 1 August 2023 for aggregate turnover above ₹5 croreNotification 10/2023-Central Tax, 10 May 2023
What the IRP returnsA unique Invoice Reference Number, a digitally signed e-invoice and a QR code, for B2B invoicese-invoice portal
30-day limitFrom 1 April 2025, taxpayers with AATO of ₹10 crore and above cannot report invoices older than 30 daysGSTN advisory
Below ₹10 croreNo such reporting time limit as of the advisoryGSTN advisory
Direct API on NIC IRPOffered only if turnover is ₹100 crore or more; otherwise through a GSP or ERPGSTN's IRP API guide, as on 29 November 2023
Cost of core APIsFree of cost on the IRPsGSTN's IRP API guide

Source: GST Council, notification 10/2023 and e-invoice portal and GSTN advisory on the 30-day limit and API details of all 6 IRPs, read 16 November 2026.

The direct API row surprises people. On the NIC portals, the option to register as a Direct API user appears only at ₹100 crore turnover or more, according to GSTN's comparison of the six IRPs. Some private IRPs in that same document say they are open to direct integration for all e-invoicing taxpayers. Most SMEs reach the IRP through their accounting software or a GST Suvidha Provider, and that is usually the right call.

The NIC sandbox's onboarding page also sets conditions for anyone using the API, starting with having automated invoice generation and keeping traffic free of malware, and NIC reserves the right to block users whose traffic harms the system.

For integration design, the 30-day rule is the one that bites. If your online orders sit in a queue because a sync failed over a long weekend and nobody noticed, a ₹10 crore business can run out of days to report them.

E-way bills from the same data

An e-way bill is needed where the value of a consignment exceeds ₹50,000, as CBIC's press note puts it. The e-way bill system has its own API, and its release notes record several rules that a sync has to respect:

  • Validity was changed from 100 km per day to 200 km per day, following a notification dated 22 December 2020.
  • From 1 January 2025, an e-way bill can only be generated within 180 days of the document date.
  • From the same date, an e-way bill cannot be extended beyond 360 days from its generation.
  • A November 2020 note says generation directly through the e-way bill system was blocked for GSTINs eligible for e-invoicing, for B2B and export invoices dated after 1 October 2020.

The last point means that for e-invoicing businesses, the e-way bill should come off the same data as the IRN, not be typed again. Zoho's e-invoicing help, for example, has separate setup paths depending on whether you generate e-way bills through Zoho Books.

Sync patterns that hold up

The format matters less than these four decisions. Make them on paper before anyone writes code.

One owner per field. Prices and stock might be owned by the ERP; customer phone numbers by the app. Write it down field by field. Two systems that both edit the same field will disagree within a week.

Push where you can, poll where you must. Zoho Books and newer SAP B1 versions can call your app with webhooks. Tally generally cannot, so a connector reads it on a schedule. Polling is fine; polling everything every minute is not.

Every write must be safe to repeat. Networks fail halfway. If your connector retries creating invoice 1042, the ERP must end up with one invoice 1042, not two. Use the order number as the key and check before you create.

Queue, log and alert. Every message goes into a queue, every failure into a log someone reads, and anything stuck longer than a few hours raises an alert. Our post on webhooks you can rely on covers the retry side in more detail.

Step by step: connecting an app or store to your ERP

Step 1. List the documents that cross over. Usually customers, items, sales orders, invoices, payments and stock. Ignore everything else for now.

Step 2. Decide the owner of each field. One table, one owner per field, signed off by the accountant.

Step 3. Check your GST position. Is your turnover above ₹5 crore in any year since 2017-18? Above ₹10 crore? Who generates the IRN and the e-way bill today?

Step 4. Pick the door. Tally: XML or JSON over HTTP through a connector on the office network, ODBC for reports. Zoho Books: REST API with OAuth plus webhooks. SAP B1: Service Layer with a session cache.

Step 5. Build against a copy. A test company in Tally, a test organisation in Zoho, a test database in SAP, and the IRP sandbox. Never test against live books.

Step 6. Run both in parallel for a month. Keep entering data the old way and compare totals daily. Switch off the manual path only when they match.

Step 7. Hand over the runbook. Who to call when the queue backs up, how to replay a failed invoice, and where the credentials live, in your name.

Three worked examples

The businesses and volumes below are illustrative, made up to show the method. They are not real customers.

A D2C brand on Shopify and TallyPrime

A brand sells about 150 orders a day online and keeps books in TallyPrime on an office PC. Its turnover is under ₹5 crore, so no e-invoicing yet.

The pipe: a small connector on the office network reads paid orders from the store each hour and posts sales vouchers to Tally through the HTTP port, using the store order number as the voucher reference so a retry never duplicates. Stock stays owned by the store; Tally gets totals. The accountant gets a daily mismatch report.

What this tells you: for Tally, the connector's location is the design decision. If the PC is off, nothing syncs, so the alert for a stuck queue matters more than any code. Shopify work often starts with exactly this.

A distributor with a sales app on Zoho Books

A distributor has 25 field salespeople taking orders on a mobile app and runs Zoho Books Professional. Turnover is above ₹5 crore, so B2B invoices need an IRN.

The pipe: the app creates sales orders in Zoho Books through the API, Zoho's own e-invoicing pushes invoices to the IRP, and a webhook tells the app when an invoice is created so the salesperson can share it. At 5,000 calls a day on Professional, the app cannot fetch the full price list on every screen; it caches items and refreshes them once a day.

What this tells you: with Zoho, the daily cap is the budget. Count calls per order before you build, and let Zoho handle the GST steps it already supports.

A manufacturer on SAP Business One with a dealer portal

A manufacturer runs SAP Business One on its own server and wants dealers to see stock, place orders and download invoices online. Turnover is above ₹10 crore, so the 30-day IRP limit applies.

The pipe: a portal backend holds one Service Layer session per company database, reads stock through OData queries, and creates sales orders. Invoices and IRNs stay in SAP, through the partner's e-invoicing add-on. Webhooks, if the version supports them, update the portal when an order changes. A daily check lists any invoice older than 20 days without an IRN.

What this tells you: for SAP, keep tax steps inside SAP and keep the portal thin. The 30-day rule turns a sync failure into a compliance problem, so the IRN age check is the most important report on the portal.

Seven common failures

Duplicate invoices on retry. The connector timed out, retried and created the voucher twice. Fix: an idempotency key, usually the source order number.

Master data drift. A party or stock item is renamed in the ERP and every later sync fails to match. Fix: sync by ID or code, never by name.

Tally closed, company not open. The HTTP port does not answer. Fix: alert on silence, not only on errors.

Rate limits hit at month end. Zoho returns 429 on the busiest day. Fix: batch, cache masters and spread retries.

Expired sessions and tokens. SAP sessions time out and Zoho access tokens need refreshing. Fix: refresh on 401 and log it.

GST rounding and HSN mismatches. The store rounds tax per line, the ERP per invoice, and the IRP rejects the difference. Fix: agree one rounding rule and send the ERP's figures to the IRP.

Late IRNs. A queue backs up and invoices age past 30 days. Fix: a daily report of invoices without an IRN, by age.

A monthly 30-minute reconciliation

Same day each month, after the books close.

A monthly integration check, split across 30 minutes

TimeWhat to checkWhat you write down
First 10 minutesOrder count and value in the app or store against invoices in the ERPAny gap and the orders behind it
Next 5 minutesFailed and retried messages in the integration logRepeat failures to fix at the source
Next 5 minutesInvoices without an IRN, by ageAnything near the 30-day limit
Next 5 minutesAPI usage against plan limitsWhether you need a bigger plan or fewer calls
Last 5 minutesCredentials, tokens and certificates due to expireWho renews them and when

Source: Zoho Books API limits and GSTN advisory on the 30-day limit, read 16 November 2026.

If you want the integration scoped and priced before anyone builds it, our ₹3,500 requirement analysis is a call with the people who would build it, the requirements worked through, and a written fixed quotation and timeline (how it works). Code, cloud and credentials stay in your name. Our ERP software page describes the wider work.
